Photograph: AP Central African Republic More than 100 dead after goldmine collapses in Central African Republic The collapse was caused by a landslide, while local officials say the death toll is likely to rise as recovery efforts continue Eromo Egbejule in Cotonou and news agencies Wed 19 Aug 2026 20.14 EDT Last modified on Wed 19 Aug 2026 20.15 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google More than 100 people have died after an artisanal goldmine at a small village in western Central African Republic (CAR) caved in due to a landslide, local officials and aid workers said on Wednesday. The landslide happened on Tuesday afternoon in the village of Zamboye, about 50km (31 miles) from the town of Baboua and close to the border of Cameroon . Footage on social media appeared to show an avalanche of sand descend on a group of people, likely the miners, and cover them. A statement by a local public prosecutor said many others were trapped under the deluge. It did not mention the number of fatalities. However, Gervais Ganagoroh, a Red Cross volunteer involved in the relief effort, told the Associated Press news agency on Wednesday that more than 100 bodies had been recovered from the collapse and ⁠a senior official at a local mining association confirmed that number to Reuters. ‘We’re hungry, there are no jobs’: a South African township’s desperate gold rush Read more Local media in CAR reported that authorities had launched an investigation into the incident. A second prosecutor from Baboua told the press that the incident is believed to have been caused by “the collapse of several underground tunnels in which miners were operating”. “The ground completely collapsed and buried people,” Cedric Mbango, a miner at the site, told the AFP news agency, describing the incident as “catastrophic”. Rescuers are racing to retrieve the bodies of victims and find survivors among the miners, believed to be nationals of CAR and Cameroon. Authorities in Cameroon’s Eastern region said at least three of its citizens have been identified as victims in the incident. Grégoire Mvongo, the region’s governor told state-owned radio on Wednesday that he was “working in close collaboration with our Central African colleagues to deal with the aftermath of this tragedy”. Bertrand Be Yangué, a member of the Zamboye youth council, said that “finding them alive would be a miracle.” He added: “We are saddened and heartbroken to see young men and women perish after coming to the mines to save their families from despair.” The toll is expected to rise as the rescue efforts continue, added Yangué. The Central African news website Corbeau News reported that heavy machinery, including tractors, was being used in the retrieval mission and could jeopardise the rescue of those still alive under the landmass. The exact number of people who were in the mine at the time of the cave-in remains unknown. Small scale artisanal mines are common in different parts of Africa, despite regulations criminalising them, as unemployment continues to drive able-bodied men to abandoned or unused mines, to eke a living. The mining sites often operate with weak safety standards leading to repeated incidents: at least 40 people have died in several mining incidents in CAR this year alone. At Milan Fashion Week, Dakota Johnson flaunted her coffee-inspired look to her nails that can easily be described as “brown sugar espresso” nails. The rich shade is perfect for fall and is a big change from the soft, neutral nail colors she usually wears. She also recently changed her hair to a darker brown shade that her colorist Tracey Cunningham called “glossed espresso.” Dakota Johnson was back—in black—at Vogue World 2026: Milano. The star arrived at the runway-show spectacle wearing witchy layers of transparent lace and chiffon from Valentino’s fall 2026 collection, titled Interferenze and designed by her good friend Alessandro Michele.134484601Dakota Johnson has been opting darker nail colors lately, and she is not the only celebrity embracing the trend. Anne Hathaway recently wore a “cherry cocoa” manicure. Gaëlle Lebrat-Personnaz, CEO of Manucurist Paris, said that brown nails could become one of the biggest manicure trends this fall. “Brown is always a beautiful color to have during autumn,” she said. “It’s an elevated nude.” The warm brown shade also has a cozy feel because it reminds people of coffee, chocolate and caramel. The brown nails can easily go with fall outfits, whether you're wearing a chunky sweater or heading out for a pumpkin patch or a walk to see the changing leaves.ALSO READ: Toshisuke Kanazawa, 90-year-old Japanese bodybuilder who beat age once drank 6 protein shakes a day, competed with Arnold SchwarzeneggerHow to get Dakota Johnson’s ‘Brown Sugar Espresso’The good news is that Johnson's manicure is easy to recreate at home. The key is choosing the right brown shade. Johnson went for a rich brown with slightly warm undertones, rather than a very dark or cool brown. To recreate the look, start with a clear base coat. Apply two coats of an opaque chestnut-brown nail polish and finish with a glossy topcoat. You can recreate the look with shades such as Manucurist Nail Polish in Chestnut, essie Nail Polish in Save a Cowboy or OPI Nail Lacquer in My Italian is a Little Rusty. Photograph: Rebecca Black/PA Belfast Man in Belfast charged with possessing explosives and firearms The 35-year-old was charged after police searched properties in Shankill Road and Edwina Street areas Nadeem Badshah Sat 31 Oct 2026 16.21 EDT Last modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 16.31 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A man has been charged under the Explosives Act and Firearms Order after police searched properties in Belfast. The 35-year-old was charged with offences including two counts of possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances, and possession of a prohibited weapon (discharge of electricity or noxious gas). He is due to appear before Belfast magistrates court on Monday, the Police Service of Northern Ireland said. The charges follow searches at properties in the Shankill Road and Edwina Street areas of north Belfast on Friday and Saturday. DCI McCallum said: “Following these searches a number of suspicious devices, along with other items, were located and seized by officers for forensic examination. “Local residents who were evacuated as a precaution have now been allowed to return home following the public safety operation conducted alongside ammunition technical officers. “All cordons have now been lifted from the area, and we thank local residents for their patience as inquiries were conducted yesterday and into today.” McCallum added: “As we continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding this incident, we would appeal to anyone who may have information that could assist with inquiries to contact us on 101, quoting reference number 261 30/10/26.” Explore more on these topics Belfast Northern Ireland news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://www.novinky.cz/clanek/zahranicni.text: Chcete-li článek poslouchat, přihlaste se Ruský soud v Kaliningradu ve čtvrtek poslal na 12 let za mříže místní právničku Mariji Bonclerovou, jež byla obviněná z vlastizrady. Soud se konal s vyloučením veřejnosti a médií, soudce zbavil obžalovanou jejích obhájců a vykázal i samu obžalovanou, s výjimkou posledního slova, uvedl server RBK. Rozsudek není pravomocný, odsouzená se může odvolat, dodal. Ruská právnička Marija Bonclerová u soudu v Kaliningradu „Odsoudit nevinného člověka je strašlivý zločin, a proto se budu modlit za své katy, aby bůh byl k nim milosrdný,“ prohlásila Bonclerová po vynesení rozsudku podle serveru Meduza. Připomněl, že 66letá advokátka proslula tím, že vystupovala jako obhájkyně v politických kauzách. „Na nohou mě drží už jen samolibost. Bojím se, že to skončí špatně,“ řekla o prudkém zhoršení svého zdravotního stavu během vyšetřovací vazby. Podle obhajoby málem zemřela na samotce kvůli podání špatných léků. Obžaloba tvrdila, že advokátka od předloňského roku shromažďovala údaje o příslušnících bezpečnostních složek, kteří odhalovali a vyšetřovali případy vedené proti lidem spolupracujícím s nikoli přátelskými státy. Tyto údaje podle obžaloby předávala člověku označenému za pracovníka ukrajinské tajné služby SBU. Obžaloba navrhla soudu potrestat advokátku 15 lety vězení. Podle ochránců lidských práv advokátku obvinili z předávání údajů, které jsou dostupné v otevřených soudních zdrojích. Konečná formulace obžaloby se také změnila z „předávala“ na „mohla předat“, upozornil server RBK a připomněl, že Bonclerová byla v červnu 2022 odsouzena k pokutě 60 000 rublů (asi 16 000 Kč) za to, že se ve svých vystoupeních před soudem dopustila „diskreditace ruské armády“, tedy kritizovala ruské tažení proti Ukrajině.
